eid_r.declaration: EvE has no native evaluator identity (native_scheme=none): the evaluator is whichever shell step evaluation.steps names, and EvE hands that step exactly EVE_WORKSPACE_ROOT, EVE_SOLVER_ROOT, EVE_EVAL_LOG_ROOT and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and no evaluator parameters (workflow/evaluation.py:290-318). The adapter pins EID* by overriding evaluation.steps with a generated step that invokes the frozen E* by absolute path and writes EID* and PINS_SHA256 into the log root it is handed. EID_r.value = 'sha256:' + sha256("a0/eve/eid_r/v1" || 0x00 || canonical_json(payload)) with payload = {schema, eid_star, native_scheme, mapping_mode, evaluator_source{digest,files}, fr_spec_hash}: eid_star is an argument of the hash, so a different EID* necessarily gives a different EID_r. Recompute from the published inputs alone with runtimes/eve/tools/recompute-eid-r (recipe: eid_r.derivation in the conformance document).

derivation.algorithm: value = 'sha256:' + sha256("a0/eve/eid_r/v1" || 0x00 || canonical_json(payload)); canonical_json = json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'), ensure_ascii=True, allow_nan=False) encoded ascii (a0/contract/evalcontract.py::canonical_json)

traces_note: Record repaired three times on 2026-09-20, always by re-materializing derived fields of the SAME events; the run was never re-executed, so every A0.1/A0.2 number in this document is the one the frozen run produced (the sampler RNG is unseeded, so a re-run would not reproduce them). (1) Trace partition: the 14 score events the pre-fix writer copied into the selection stream were removed and the merged all.jsonl written from the three per-kind files in event_seq order. (2) EID_r derivation (audit R3): every event's eid_r block was replaced with the value derived from EID* by a0_adapter/eidmap.py. (3) failure_stage (adapter_contract.md §4.5): the nine non-ok C* units were restaged with the adopted frozen A0-wide table (failure_stage_mapping digest 201fed78...), which changes {resolve_failed: 9} into {verify_failed: 5, resolve_failed: 1, evaluator_failed: 2, timeout: 1}; the a01 counter keys `evaluator_failed`/`resolve_failed` were renamed to `value_mismatch`/`runtime_failed_a_measurable_candidate` so they cannot be mistaken for stage counts, and a01.candidates gained the reference_outcome_* / failure_stage fields the current code emits. Re-serialization was verified byte-identical for every unchanged field. See README.md 'FailureStage accounting' and 'FailureStage counts and trace paths'.
